newsitem.title: CANADA: Hibernia partners to transship via Newfoundland.
newsitem.headline: Hibernia partners to transship via Newfoundland.

text.p: Partners in the Hibernia project said on Thursday they agreed to transship Hibernia crude oil that is not directly shipped to market, using transshipment facilities to be built in Newfoundland.

Mobil Oil Canada Properties, Chevron Canada Resources and Petro-Canada said they would form a company that would own and construct a crude oil transshipment terminal in Newfoundland. The terminal would be located on the Avalon Peninsula at Whiffin Head, they said.
The decision followed a review of options to transport crude oil from Hibernia and other Grand Banks crude oil developments directly to market using three or more shuttle tankers.
Mobil Oil Canada president Jerry Anderson said he was pleased the group would build the facility in Newfoundland. He said the system would help to ensure the production can be competitively marketed.
The facility will have a minimum of one berth for the tankers, capable of being expanded to two or more berths as needed, which will accommodate crude oil tankers up to 155,000 dead weight tons.
The heated crude oil storage facilities will have a capacity of at least 1.5 million barrels with provision to expand to accommodate future Grand Banks production.
Norm McIntyre, executive vice-president of Petro-Canada, said the terminal provided the last component of the transportation infrastructure requirements for the Hibernia project.
"With Hibernia about to come on stream and substantial progress made on Terra Nova, the construction of this facility supports Petro Canada's east coast growth strategy," McIntyre said.

The companies said final cost estimates for the regional terminal were not completed, but that the terminal was anticipated to cost more than $100 million for the Hibernia project's requirements alone.

They said a contract had been awarded to an alliance team of Bantrel Inc of Calgary, Sandwell Inc of Vancouver and Newfoundland Design Associates of St. John's, Newfoundland to provide engineering design, procurement and construction management services for the project. Expenditures during the preliminary engineering phase of the project are anticipated to be about C$10 million.

During the construction phase, expected to begin in spring 1997, the average number of jobs will be about 150 with a peak of about 300. The operations phase, to begin in the autumn of 1998, will provide long-term employment opportunities for about 20 to 40 people.
Participants in the regional transshipment terminal project include Mobil (41 percent), Chevron (34 percent) and Petro-Canada (25 percent).

Participants in the Hibernia project are Mobil Oil Canada (33.125 percent), Chevron Canada Resources (26.875 percent), Petro-Canada (25 percent), Canada Hibernia Holding Corporation (8.5 percent) and Murphy Atlantic Offshore Oil Company Ltd. (6.5 percent).
